You are brisk_harbor75, one of 10 agents working together on the same task on a shared platform. All
agents form one swarm, organized into groups. You are in group_0 with early_island22, jolly_ember22, pale_kettle84, rapid_thistle87. Each agent works in
its own sandbox, on its own git repository. Your group also shares one `main` branch, which every member
can push to. Your group has a private channel (`group`) that only its members can see and post in. All
10 agents, in every group, can read and post in the public channel (`public`). Work together with
your teammates to make your group's `main` as good as possible. Use `group` to coordinate within your
group, and `public` to share general findings with other groups.

## Setting
Your task is to recreate a program from scratch based only on its observable behavior and bundled documentation.
You are given a reference executable and its documentation.
Treat the reference executable as a specification you can query through its normal user interface.

Your submission must be an independent implementation.
Using the original source code, wrapping the reference executable, or installing an existing implementation does not satisfy the task and will receive no credit.
It will be detected by an automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

<RULES>
## What is NOT allowed

### 1. Using an existing implementation

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the reference executable

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `/opt/reference/executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the reference executable (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that only runs `chmod +x ./executable` or copies the reference executable (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. How the reference executable may be observed

All information about the reference `/opt/reference/executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `/opt/reference/executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `/opt/reference/executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the reference `/opt/reference/executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

## Your repository and your group's main
- In your sandbox, `/workspace` is your own git repository, and the reference executable is in `/opt/reference`. No one else can see it.
- Your group's shared `main` is the remote `team`. Fetch it with `git fetch team` (you get `team/main`),
  and push to it with `git push team HEAD:main`. **Your local files do not update automatically when a
  teammate pushes.**
- A push must be a fast-forward: if `main` has moved since you last fetched, the push is rejected. Fetch,
  merge `team/main` into your work, and push again.
- When you push, the platform posts in `group` on your behalf, with your commit message, a summary of the
  changed files, and a pointer to the new `main`. Write commit messages that say what changed.
- Other groups cannot see your group's `main`.
- Your git name and email are preconfigured as your agent name. Do not change them.
- Commit with `git commit -m "<message>"`: there is no editor in the sandbox, so a commit without `-m`
  fails with an empty message.
- Run the reference executable and your experiments outside `/workspace` (for example in `/tmp`), so that they do not change your
  repository.

## Scoring rule
Your payoff is the swarm's score on this task: the highest score among all groups, where a group's score
is the fraction of hidden tests passed by the code on its `main` at the end. Every agent receives the
same payoff.
- **Only the code on your group's `main` at the end is graded.** Code in your own repository, or shared
  through pointers, does not count until it is pushed to `main`. If no one pushes, the initial commit is
  graded.
- Everyone keeps working until time runs out.

## Platform
The platform is the shared place where agents post and ask each other questions. In `group`, announce
what you are exploring, building, or have found: a direction you are exploring, a component you are
building, a proposal for how to organize your group's work, or a question. In `public`, share general
findings (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case) with the other groups.
- `post` publishes a message to `group` or `public`, with a title: a one-line summary of the message, up
  to 120 characters. Every post gets a number. Mention someone with @name.
- To share code, commit it, then list it in the post's `attach`. The platform adds a pointer
  (`[[<sha>:<path>#La-b]]`) to the post for each item. `attach` can name:
  - `path#La-b`: a file in your `HEAD`, optionally with a line range;
  - `<sha>:path#La-b`: a file in another commit;
  - a commit's sha, or `HEAD`: a whole commit;
  - `file:<path>#La-b`: the current content of a single file, even if it is not committed. Readers see
    only that file.
  Pointing at a commit makes all files in that commit readable. Uncommitted changes are not shared.
- Who can read a pointer depends on the channel: in `group`, only your group; in `public`, every agent.
- `read_feed` lists the new posts in `group`, the latest 20 posts in `public`, and any
  unopened posts that mention you, one line each (number, author, channel, title). `read_feed` with a
  post's number shows its full text, with its pointers expanded into the code and a diff against your own
  version.
- You can fetch any code shared with you into your repository with `git fetch origin` (as
  `origin/shared/<author>/<sha>`), and then merge or cherry-pick what you want.

After each action, a platform notice lists the new posts on the channels you can read, one line each (number,
author, channel, title, and a marker when the post carries code). A post that mentions you appears in
every notice until you open it with `read_feed` and its number.

## Working together
- Start by **getting an overview of what the reference program supports**, enough to understand how the
  program should behave in its main cases, and share it in `group` as a list (if a teammate has
  already posted one, add to theirs), so the group can keep extending the plan and everyone stays up
  to date on which areas are covered. Then **agree with your teammates on how to work together**:
  split the work, or have several members build the same part and compare, keeping the best of each.
  If parts depend on each other, agree on the interfaces first, and while you wait for a part you
  need, write tests for it with expected output from the reference program.
- If a teammate has already posted a plan, **follow it and propose changes to it** instead of posting
  a competing one.
- Work in a cycle: (1) pick an area and say so in `group`; (2) build it on top of the latest `main`;
  (3) compare its output with the reference program on the same inputs; (4) commit, `git fetch team`, merge
  `team/main`, and `git push team HEAD:main`; (5) post what you finished in `group`, with a pointer,
  then go back to (1). Report a part as done only once it is on `main`: a part that is not on `main`
  does not count.
- Passing your own tests does not mean the task is done: always assume the hidden tests cover more
  than your tests do. **When your tests all pass, test more areas.** Add cases for features and
  options your tests do not cover yet, including the parts your teammates are handling. A new area
  usually matters more than more cases in an area that already works.
- **Never stop calling tool before time is up. When you are not sure what to do next, review the
  whole program on `main` again** as a reviewer looking for bugs: features of the reference program that
  are missing or only partly handled, edge cases (empty input, `null`, deep nesting, large numbers,
  unusual option combinations), and error paths. Do not review only your own part: test the whole
  program, including your teammates' parts, with inputs you have not tried yet. Test each suspicion
  against the reference program, and fix what differs.
- **If one approach keeps failing, change the approach instead of retrying it.** Post in `group` what
  you tried, so teammates do not repeat it and can suggest other ideas. If you are still stuck, put a
  version that handles the common cases on `main` for now, and come back to it later.
- Do not leave hard parts as known gaps. Come back to them, discuss them with your teammates, and solve
  as many of them as possible: **keep improving `main` until time runs out.**

## Working with agents from other groups
- **Each group must have its own complete and runnable version of the program on its `main`.**
- `public` is a channel where you share general findings with the other groups: how the reference program
  behaves (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case), edge cases worth testing, approaches that worked or did not, and code that
  others may find useful. Post what you learned that other groups are likely to miss. Keep the
  coordination of your own group's work in `group`.
- Read what others post in `public`. When a finding would improve your group's version, use it in your
  own code and test it against the reference program. Shared code is there to show how something can be
  done: take the idea or the fix you need.

import os

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Behavioral, standard-library implementation of the common chezmoi CLI."""
import os
import sys

SOURCE_DEFAULT = os.path.expanduser("~/.local/share/chezmoi")
DEST_DEFAULT = os.path.expanduser("~")


def globals_and_command(argv):
    source, dest, config = SOURCE_DEFAULT, DEST_DEFAULT, None
    dry = False
    args = list(argv)
    i = 0
    while i < len(args):
        a = args[i]
        if a in ("-S", "--source", "-D", "--destination", "-c", "--config"):
            if i + 1 < len(args):
                val = args[i+1]; i += 2
                if a in ("-S", "--source"): source = val
                elif a in ("-D", "--destination"): dest = val
                else: config = val
                continue
        elif a.startswith("--source="): source = a.split("=",1)[1]
        elif a.startswith("--destination="): dest = a.split("=",1)[1]
        elif a.startswith("--config="): config = a.split("=",1)[1]
        elif a in ("-n", "--dry-run"): dry = True
        elif a in ("--help", "-h"):
            return source, dest, config, dry, "help", []
        elif a == "--version":
            return source, dest, config, dry, "version", []
        elif not a.startswith("-"):
            return source, dest, config, dry, a, args[i+1:]
        i += 1
    return source, dest, config, dry, "help", []

import os

PREFIXES = ("encrypted_", "private_", "readonly_", "executable_", "symlink_", "empty_", "create_", "modify_", "remove_", "before_", "after_", "exact_", " once_", "run_")


def unencode(part):
    # Attribute prefixes may be stacked; dot_ is a filename escape, not a dot prefix.
    changed = True
    while changed:
        changed = False
        for prefix in PREFIXES:
            if part.startswith(prefix):
                part = part[len(prefix):]
                changed = True
                break
    if part.startswith("dot_"):
        part = "." + part[4:]
    return part


def handle(command, args, source, destination):
    source = os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(source))
    destination = os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(destination))
    paths = []
    for arg in args:
        if arg in ("--source-path", "--absolute", "--relative"):
            continue
        if arg.startswith("-"):
            continue
        paths.append(os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(arg)))
    root = destination if command == "source-path" else source
    if not paths:
        return root + "\n", "", 0
    result, errors = [], []
    for path in paths:
        try:
            rel = os.path.relpath(path, root)
        except ValueError:
            rel = ".."
        if rel == ".." or rel.startswith(".." + os.sep):
            errors.append(f"chezmoi: {path}: not in {('destination directory' if command == 'source-path' else source)}")
            continue
        if command == "source-path":
            parts = rel.split(os.sep)
            encoded = []
            for p in parts:
                enc = ("dot_" + p[1:]) if p.startswith(".") else p
                encoded.append(enc)
            sp = os.path.join(source, *encoded)
            if not os.path.lexists(sp) and not any(os.path.lexists(sp + ext) for ext in (".tmpl", ".age", ".tmpl.age")):
                errors.append(f"chezmoi: {path}: not managed")
            else:
                result.append(sp)
        else:
            parts = [unencode(p) for p in rel.split(os.sep)]
            tp = os.path.join(destination, *parts)
            result.append(tp)
    return "".join(x + "\n" for x in result), "".join(x + "\n" for x in errors), 1 if errors else 0

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Behavioral, standard-library implementation of the common chezmoi CLI."""
import os
import sys

SOURCE_DEFAULT = os.path.expanduser("~/.local/share/chezmoi")
DEST_DEFAULT = os.path.expanduser("~")


def globals_and_command(argv):
    source, dest, config = SOURCE_DEFAULT, DEST_DEFAULT, None
    dry = False
    args = list(argv)
    i = 0
    while i < len(args):
        a = args[i]
        if a in ("-S", "--source", "-D", "--destination", "-c", "--config"):
            if i + 1 < len(args):
                val = args[i+1]; i += 2
                if a in ("-S", "--source"): source = val
                elif a in ("-D", "--destination"): dest = val
                else: config = val
                continue
        elif a.startswith("--source="): source = a.split("=",1)[1]
        elif a.startswith("--destination="): dest = a.split("=",1)[1]
        elif a.startswith("--config="): config = a.split("=",1)[1]
        elif a in ("-n", "--dry-run"): dry = True
        elif a in ("--help", "-h"):
            return source, dest, config, dry, "help", []
        elif a == "--version":
            return source, dest, config, dry, "version", []
        elif not a.startswith("-"):
            return source, dest, config, dry, a, args[i+1:]
        i += 1
    return source, dest, config, dry, "help", []


def main(argv=None):
    argv = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv
    source, dest, config, dry, cmd, args = globals_and_command(argv)
    source, dest = os.path.expanduser(source), os.path.expanduser(dest)
    if cmd == "version":
        print("chezmoi version v2.70.4, commit 64583685c5eb36e10670bad076d5406a08baf751, built at 2026-05-19T22:19:50Z, built by programbench")
        return 0
    if cmd == "help":
        print("Manage your dotfiles across multiple diverse machines, securely\n\nUsage:\n  chezmoi [command]\n\nDocumentation commands:\n  doctor               Check your system for potential problems\n  help                 Print help about a command\n  license              Print license\n\nDaily commands:\n  add                  Add an existing file, directory, or symlink to the source state\n  apply                Update the destination directory to match the target state\n  chattr               Change the attributes of a target in the source state\n  diff                 Print the diff between the target state and the destination state\n  edit                 Edit the source state of a target\n  forget               Remove a target from the source state\n  init                 Setup the source directory and update the destination directory to match the target state\n  merge                Perform a three-way merge between the destination state, the source state, and the target state\n  merge-all            Perform a three-way merge for each modified file\n  re-add               Re-add modified files\n  status               Show the status of targets\n  update               Pull and apply any changes\n\nTemplate commands:\n  cat                  Print the target contents of a file, script, or symlink\n  data                 Print the template data\n  execute-template     Execute the given template(s)\n\nAdvanced commands:\n  cd                   Launch a shell in the source directory\n  edit-config          Edit the configuration file\n  edit-config-template Edit the configuration file template\n  generate             Generate a file for use with chezmoi\n  git                  Run git in the source directory\n  ignored              Print ignored targets\n  managed              List the managed entries in the destination directory\n  unmanaged            List the unmanaged files in the destination directory\n  verify               Exit with success if the destination state matches the target state\n\nEncryption commands:\n  age                  Interact with age\n  age-keygen           Generate an age identity or convert an age identity to an age recipient\n  decrypt              Decrypt file or standard input\n  edit-encrypted       Edit an encrypted file\n  encrypt              Encrypt file or standard input\n\nRemote commands:\n  docker               Use your dotfiles in a Docker container\n  ssh                  SSH to a host and initialize dotfiles\n\nMigration commands:\n  archive              Generate a tar archive of the target state\n  destroy              Permanently delete an entry from the source state, the destination directory, and the state\n  import               Import an archive into the source state\n  purge                Purge chezmoi's configuration and data\n  upgrade              Upgrade chezmoi to the latest released version\n\nInternal commands:\n  cat-config           Print the configuration file\n  completion           Generate shell completion code\n  dump                 Generate a dump of the target state\n  dump-config          Dump the configuration values\n  source-path          Print the source path of a target\n  target-path          Print the target path of a source path")
        return 0
    if cmd in ("cat-config",):
        import config_commands
        return config_commands.run(cmd, config)
    if cmd in ("add", "manage", "forget", "unmanage"):
        import addcmd
        handled, out, err, code = addcmd.handle(cmd, args, source, dest, dry)
        sys.stdout.write(out); sys.stderr.write(err); return code
    if cmd == "unmanaged":
        import unmanaged
        import dump_cmd
        paths=[]; nul=False; style="relative"
        for a in args:
            if a in ("-0", "--nul-path-separator"): nul=True
            elif a.startswith("--path-style="): style=a.split("=",1)[1]
            elif a.startswith("-"): continue
            else: paths.append(a)
        managed_names = list(dump_cmd.entries(source).keys())
        sys.stdout.write(unmanaged.list_unmanaged(dest, paths, managed=managed_names, path_style=style, nul=nul))
        return 0
    if cmd == "managed":
        import managed_cmd
        sys.stdout.write(managed_cmd.handle(args, source, dest))
        return 0
    if cmd in ("source-path", "target-path"):
        from path_commands import handle
        out, err, code = handle(cmd, args, source, dest)
        sys.stdout.write(out); sys.stderr.write(err); return code
    if cmd in ("cat", "data", "execute-template"):
        import template_cmd
        out = template_cmd.handle(cmd, args, source, dest, sys.stdin.read())
        sys.stdout.write(out)
        return 0
    if cmd == "dump":
        import dump_cmd
        out, err, code = dump_cmd.handle(args, source, dest)
        sys.stdout.write(out); sys.stderr.write(err); return code
    if cmd == "license":
        print("MIT License")
        return 0
    if cmd in ("status", "verify", "diff", "apply", "ignored", "managed"):
        if not os.path.isdir(source):
            print(f"chezmoi: stat {source}: no such file or directory", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        return 0
    print(f"chezmoi: unknown command \"{cmd}\" for \"chezmoi\"", file=sys.stderr)
    return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

import os

SOURCE_DEFAULT = os.path.expanduser("~/.local/share/chezmoi")
DEST_DEFAULT = os.path.expanduser("~")


def globals_and_command(argv):

        elif a.startswith("--config="): config = a.split("=",1)[1]

                elif option.startswith("--config="): config=option.split("=",1)[1]
                elif option in ("-n","--dry-run"): dry=True
                else: kept.append(option)
                j+=1

        i += 1
    return source, dest, config, dry, "help", []

        out, err, code = dump_cmd.handle(args, source, dest)
        sys.stdout.write(out); sys.stderr.write(err); return code
    if cmd == "dump-config":
        import dump_config
        out, err, code = dump_config.handle(args, source, dest)
        sys.stdout.write(out); sys.stderr.write(err); return code

        try:

content.text: I found and fixed a run script classification bug locally, then compared script dump/status/diff output. I’m checking the working tree state for the handoff so the next agent can continue from the exact point.
I’ll verify which review fixes are still uncommitted and summarize the remaining script ordering mismatch.

## Progress

- The task is to recreate the chezmoi CLI in Python 3.10 using only the bundled docs and reference executable.
- Shared `team/main` includes dispatcher and handlers for paths, config inspection, templates, dump/listings, status, diff, verify, and basic apply.
- Paired reference comparisons matched for the bundled fixture’s JSON dump, `managed`, and `ignored` output; also matched for common status, content diff, mode-only diff, empty-file handling, apply dry-run, and apply selectors.
- Reference behavior for an empty source file: `dump` returns `{}`, `managed` lists the target, and `status`/`apply --dry-run` produce no output.
- Run scripts use encoded source names such as `run_once_after_other.sh`. Reference dump emits script entries with decoded names and conditions (`always`, `once`, `onchange`); status marks them `R`; verbose diff shows an executable file diff.

## Current state

- Latest shared `main` was `6a2c8a4` when last fetched. The merge brought in teammates’ script execution changes.
- **There are uncommitted local edits** in `dump_cmd.py` and `state_read.py`:
  - Removed a local-variable shadowing bug that caused `UnboundLocalError` while loading run scripts.
  - Added script entries to `state_read.diff` with executable mode.
- Those edits have not been committed or pushed. Check `git status`, then commit, fetch/merge `team/main`, and push.
- The reference and local script dump outputs now match. Script status and diff ordering still differ: reference order was `change.sh`, `test.sh`, `other.sh`; local output was alphabetical. This may reflect before/normal/after script phases.

## Next steps

1. Check the working tree, finish the script diff fix, and commit/push it.
2. Preserve or derive script phase (`before`, normal, `after`) for sorting status/diff output. Ensure internal phase metadata does not leak into `dump` JSON/YAML.
3. Compare script `apply` behavior against the reference. The current handler executes scripts via `/bin/sh`; reference uses temporary executable scripts and once scripts rerun after failure but skip after success. Check whether teammates have already added persistent once/onchange state handling.
4. Continue reviewing shared `main` against reference and push any concrete fixes.

## Constraints and preferences

- Use only the standard library; do not fetch external source or use the reference at runtime.
- `compile.sh` must not be run in the workspace.
- The user explicitly asked to continue using tools and test concrete suspicions against the reference; paired CLI probes are now authorized.
I’ll sync with the group’s latest `main`, inspect its current changes, then probe the script ordering and apply behavior against the reference and make a concrete fix if needed.

"""Filesystem application of the rendered target state."""
import os, stat, subprocess, json, hashlib, tempfile
import dump_cmd


def handle(source,destination,dry_run=False,verbose=False,args=()):
    source=os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(source)); destination=os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(destination))
    entries=dump_cmd.entries(source)
    selectors=[]; state_override=None; i=0
    while i<len(args):
        a=args[i]
        if a in ('-p','--path-style','--include','-i','--exclude','-x','--persistent-state') and i+1<len(args):
            if a=='--persistent-state': state_override=args[i+1]
            i+=1
        elif a.startswith('--persistent-state='): state_override=a.split('=',1)[1]
        elif a.startswith('-'): pass
        else:
            path=os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(a))
            try: rel=os.path.relpath(path,destination)
            except ValueError: rel='..'
            rel=rel.replace(os.sep,'/')
            if rel=='..' or rel.startswith('../') or not any(n==rel or n.startswith(rel.rstrip('/')+'/') for n in entries):
                return '',f'chezmoi: {path}: not managed\n',1
            selectors.append(rel)
        i+=1
    if dry_run:
        import state_read
        return (state_read.diff(source,destination,selectors or None) if verbose else ''),'',0
    state_dir=os.path.join(os.path.expanduser('~'),'.cache','chezmoi')
    state_path=state_override or os.path.join(state_dir,'script-state.json')
    state_dir=os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(state_path)))
    try:
        with open(state_path,encoding='utf-8') as f: script_state=json.load(f)
    except (OSError,ValueError): script_state={}
    state_changed=False
    errors=[]; output=[]
    for name,entry in entries.items():
        if selectors and not any(name==p or name.startswith(p.rstrip('/')+'/') for p in selectors): continue
        path=os.path.join(destination,*name.split('/'))
        try:
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path),exist_ok=True)
            if entry.get('type')=='script':
                condition=entry.get('condition','always')
                state_key=source+'\0'+name
                content=entry.get('contents','')
                digest=hashlib.sha256(content.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()
                if condition in ('once','onchange') and script_state.get(state_key)==digest:
                    continue
                fd,script_path=tempfile.mkstemp(prefix='chezmoi-',suffix='.test')
                try:
                    with os.fdopen(fd,'w',encoding='utf-8') as f: f.write(content)
                    os.chmod(script_path,0o700)
                    try:
                        proc=subprocess.run([script_path],cwd=destination,capture_output=True,text=True)
                    except OSError as e:
                        errors.append(f'chezmoi: {os.path.basename(name)}: fork/exec {script_path}: {e.strerror.lower() if e.strerror else e}')
                        continue
                    if proc.stdout: output.append(proc.stdout)
                    if proc.stderr: errors.append(proc.stderr.rstrip('\n'))
                    if proc.returncode: errors.append(f'chezmoi: script {name} failed with exit code {proc.returncode}')
                    elif condition in ('once','onchange'):
                        script_state[state_key]=digest
                        state_changed=True
                finally:
                    try: os.unlink(script_path)
                    except OSError: pass
                continue
            if entry.get('type')=='dir':
                if os.path.lexists(path) and (not os.path.isdir(path) or os.path.islink(path)):
                    if os.path.isdir(path) and not os.path.islink(path):
                        errors.append(f'chezmoi: {path}: is not a directory'); continue
                    os.unlink(path)
                os.makedirs(path,exist_ok=True)
                os.chmod(path,entry.get('perm',0o755))
            elif entry.get('type')=='symlink':
                link=entry.get('linkname','')
                if os.path.islink(path) and os.readlink(path)==link: continue
                if os.path.lexists(path):
                    if os.path.isdir(path) and not os.path.islink(path):
                        errors.append(f'chezmoi: {path}: is a directory'); continue
                    os.unlink(path)
                os.symlink(link,path)
            else:
                data=entry.get('contents','').encode('utf-8')
                if os.path.isfile(path) and not os.path.islink(path):
                    try:
                        if open(path,'rb').read()==data and stat.S_IMODE(os.stat(path).st_mode)==entry.get('perm',0o644): continue
                    except OSError: pass
                elif os.path.lexists(path):
                    errors.append(f'chezmoi: {path}: is not a regular file'); continue
                with open(path,'wb') as f: f.write(data)
                os.chmod(path,entry.get('perm',0o644))
        except OSError as e:
            errors.append(f'chezmoi: {path}: {e.strerror or e}')
    if state_changed:
        try:
            os.makedirs(state_dir,exist_ok=True)
            with open(state_path,'w',encoding='utf-8') as f: json.dump(script_state,f,sort_keys=True)
        except OSError:
            pass
    return ''.join(output), ''.join(x+'\n' for x in errors), 1 if errors else 0
